subproblems.title: Mass of a restriction is at most the mass of the current on W ⊂⊂ U
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContainedOpen W U: W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U), A ⊆ ℝ^P, and X, S ∈ D_k(U) such that S is a restriction of X to A (IsRestriction X A S). Then M_W(S) ≤ M_W(X).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U W A : Set (Eucl P)) (X S : GeometricCurrentOn U k), IsOpen U → CompactlyContainedOpen W U → IsRestriction X A S → S.massOn W ≤ X.massOn W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1, display (∗), of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, (2.8)–(2.9): M_W(T ⌞ A) = μ_T(W ∩ A) ≤ μ_T(W) = M_W(T)).

Conventions. (R0) and (R2) denote the first and third conjuncts of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.iwl_restriction_theory (its frozen type is byte-identical in dag.json):
- (R0) if X ∈ D_k(U), U open, has a measure representation (IsMeasureRepresentation X μ v), then M_V(X) < ∞ for every V with CompactlyContainedOpen V U;
- (R2) if U is open and M_V(X) < ∞ for every V ⊂⊂ U, then there is a measure μ with IsMassMeasure X μ such that X has a restriction to every measurable set and every restriction S′ of X to any set A′ satisfies M_{W′}(S′) = μ(W′ ∩ A′) for every open W′ ⊆ U.

1. Unfold IsRestriction X A S. A is measurable, and there are a measure μ and v : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) with IsMeasureRepresentation X μ v (and S(ω) = ∫_A ⟨ω, v⟩ dμ for every test form ω). Keep the hypothesis IsRestriction X A S itself for step 4.
2. By (R0), applied to U (open), X, μ and v: M_V(X) < ∞ for every V with CompactlyContainedOpen V U.
3. By (R2), applied to U and X (whose local masses are finite by step 2), there is a measure μ_X such that:
 - IsMassMeasure X μ_X holds, i.e. μ_X(U^c) = 0 and μ_X(V) = M_V(X) for every V ⊂⊂ U;
 - M_{W′}(S′) = μ_X(W′ ∩ A′) for every restriction S′ of X to a set A′ and every open W′ ⊆ U.
4. W is open (first component of CompactlyContainedOpen W U), and W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U (subset_closure and the third component). Applying the formula of step 3 to S′ := S, A′ := A and W′ := W gives M_W(S) = μ_X(W ∩ A).
5. W ∩ A ⊆ W, so μ_X(W ∩ A) ≤ μ_X(W) by monotonicity of measures (measure_mono). Also μ_X(W) = M_W(X) by the second component of IsMassMeasure X μ_X applied to W, since W ⊂⊂ U.
6. Combining steps 4 and 5: M_W(S) = μ_X(W ∩ A) ≤ μ_X(W) = M_W(X). ∎
proof_key_steps: Unpack IsRestriction X A S to obtain a measure representation (μ, v) of X.
(R0) of Submission.iwl_restriction_theory: X has finite mass on every V ⊂⊂ U.
(R2): mass measure μ_X of X with M_{W′}(S′) = μ_X(W′ ∩ A′) for every restriction S′ of X to A′ and every open W′ ⊆ U.
W is open and W ⊆ U, so M_W(S) = μ_X(W ∩ A).
μ_X(W ∩ A) ≤ μ_X(W) = M_W(X), by monotonicity and IsMassMeasure (W ⊂⊂ U).

subproblems.title: A slice of a cycle is the boundary of the corresponding restriction
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with ∂T = 0, f : ℝ^P → ℝ, t ∈ ℝ, and S ∈ D_m(U) with IsSlice T f t S (S = ∂(T ⌞ {f < t}) − (∂T) ⌞ {f < t}, with the sets taken inside U). Then there is A ∈ D_{m+1}(U) such that A is a restriction of T to {x ∈ U : f(x) < t} (IsRestriction T {x ∈ U : f(x) < t} A) and ∂A = S.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (t : ℝ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U m), IsOpen U → T.boundary = 0 → IsSlice T f t S → ∃ A : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), IsRestriction T {x | x ∈ U ∧ f x < t} A ∧ A.boundary = S
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, (4.6) with ∂T = 0).

Conventions. (R1) is the second conjunct of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.iwl_restriction_theory: if U is open, then any two restrictions (IsRestriction) of the same current X ∈ D_k(U) to the same set are equal. Write A_t := {x ∈ U : f(x) < t}.

1. Unfold IsSlice T f t S. There are A ∈ D_{m+1}(U) and B ∈ D_m(U) such that:
 (a) IsRestriction T A_t A;
 (b) IsRestriction ∂T A_t B;
 (c) S(ω) = ∂A(ω) − B(ω) for every ω ∈ D^m(U).
2. The zero current 0 ∈ D_m(U) is a restriction of ∂T to A_t:
 (i) A_t is measurable, by the first component of (b).
 (ii) Take the zero measure μ := 0 and v := 0 : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P). Then IsMeasureRepresentation ∂T 0 0 holds. For each test form ω, the function x ↦ 0(ω(x)) is integrable with respect to the zero measure, since every function is (integrable_zero_measure). Moreover ∂T(ω) = 0, because ∂T = 0 and the zero current vanishes on every form (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply), and ∫ 0(ω(x)) d0(x) = 0, an integral against the zero measure.
 (iii) For each ω, 0(ω) = 0 = ∫_{A_t} 0(ω(x)) d0(x).
3. Apply (R1) to U (open), the current ∂T ∈ D_m(U), the set A_t and its two restrictions B (from (b)) and 0 (from step 2). This gives B = 0.
4. For every ω ∈ D^m(U), (c) and step 3 give S(ω) = ∂A(ω) − 0(ω) = ∂A(ω) − 0 = ∂A(ω). By extensionality of currents (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), ∂A = S.
5. By (a), A is a restriction of T to A_t = {x ∈ U : f(x) < t}, and ∂A = S by step 4. Hence A is the required current. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold IsSlice: there are restrictions A of T and B of ∂T to A_t = {x ∈ U : f(x) < t} with S = ∂A − B.
0 is a restriction of ∂T = 0 to A_t: A_t is measurable (from B's restriction); use μ := 0, v := 0.
Hence S(ω) = ∂A(ω) for all ω, and ∂A = S by GeometricCurrentOn.ext.

subproblems.title: Restrictions of a cycle to sublevel sets with an integrable boundary-mass bound
subproblems.statement: Assume SlicingTheorem. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContainedOpen W U), and X ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with ∂X = 0 and M_V(X) < ∞ for every V ⊂⊂ U. Let d : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz (L ∈ ℝ≥0) and a < b. Then there are currents A_t ∈ D_{m+1}(U) (t ∈ ℝ) and a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] such that: (i) for every t, A_t is a restriction of X to {x ∈ U : d(x) < t}; (ii) M_W(∂A_t) ≤ g(t) for every t ∈ (a, b); (iii) ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g(t) dt ≤ L · M_W(X).
subproblems.lean_statement: SlicingTheorem → ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (d : Eucl P → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (a b : ℝ), IsOpen U → CompactlyContainedOpen W U → LipschitzWith L d → a < b → X.boundary = 0 → (∀ V, CompactlyContainedOpen V U → X.massOn V < ∞) → ∃ (A : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), Measurable g ∧ (∀ t, IsRestriction X {x | x ∈ U ∧ d x < t} (A t)) ∧ (∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, (A t).boundary.massOn W ≤ g t) ∧ ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * X.massOn W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2, 3 and 4 of the parent proof for a single cycle X (Simon Ch. 6, 4.5(1)–(2), 4.6, 4.10).

Conventions. (R2) is the third conjunct of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.iwl_restriction_theory: if U is open and M_V(X) < ∞ for every V ⊂⊂ U, then there is a measure μ with IsMassMeasure X μ such that X has a restriction to every measurable set (the accompanying mass formula is not needed here). The sibling lemmas are:
- cycle_slice_boundary (Submission.ind_pi_ss_cycle_slice_boundary);
- restriction_mass_le (Submission.ind_pi_ss_restriction_massOn_le).
For t ∈ ℝ put A_t := {x ∈ U : d(x) < t}.

1. Preliminaries.
 - W is open, and W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U (components of CompactlyContainedOpen W U).
 - d is continuous (LipschitzWith.continuous) and L-Lipschitz on U (LipschitzWith.lipschitzOnWith).
2. The zero current has zero mass. For every set V, M_V(0) = 0. By definition, M_V(0) is the supremum of ofReal(0(ω)) over the mass-admissible forms ω. Since 0(ω) = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply), every such value is ofReal 0 = 0. Hence M_V(0) ≤ 0 (sSup_le), and M_V(0) = 0.
3. Slicing.
 - For every V ⊂⊂ U, M_V(X) < ∞ by hypothesis, and M_V(∂X) = M_V(0) = 0 < ∞ by ∂X = 0 and step 2.
 - So the hypothesis of SlicingTheorem holds for T := X on U, with f := d and the constant L of step 1.
 - SlicingTheorem gives S : ℝ → D_m(U) with IsSlice X d t S_t for every t ∈ ℝ, together with its mass clause (used in step 6).
4. Slices are boundaries.
 - Fix t. Apply the sibling lemma cycle_slice_boundary to U (open), T := X (∂X = 0), f := d, t and S := S_t (IsSlice X d t S_t). It gives a current A′ with IsRestriction X A_t A′ and ∂A′ = S_t.
 - By choice, fix such an A′ =: A_t for every t ∈ ℝ.
 - Thus, for every t, A_t is a restriction of X to {x ∈ U : d(x) < t}, and ∂A_t = S_t.
5. A restriction to the band.
 - The band Bd := {x ∈ U : a < d(x) < b} = U ∩ {a < d} ∩ {d < b} is open: U is open, and {a < d} and {d < b} are open by continuity of d (isOpen_lt). Hence Bd is measurable (IsOpen.measurableSet).
 - X has finite mass on every V ⊂⊂ U. By (R2), X therefore has a restriction to every measurable set. Fix Rb with IsRestriction X Bd Rb.
6. Slice mass bound.
 - By Mathlib's norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz, ‖fderiv ℝ d x‖ ≤ L for every x ∈ ℝ^P, hence ‖fderiv ℝ d x‖₊ ≤ L for every x. So the almost-everywhere derivative hypothesis of the mass clause holds on W with L_W := L.
 - Apply the mass clause of SlicingTheorem with W (open, W ⊆ U), L_W := L, a < b and R := Rb (step 5).
 - It gives a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with M_W(S_t) ≤ g(t) for every t ∈ (a, b), and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g ≤ L · M_W(Rb).
7. Comparison with X.
 - The sibling lemma restriction_mass_le (U open, W ⊂⊂ U, IsRestriction X Bd Rb) gives M_W(Rb) ≤ M_W(X).
 - Multiplication by L in [0, ∞] is monotone, so ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g ≤ L · M_W(Rb) ≤ L · M_W(X).
8. Boundary mass bound. For t ∈ (a, b), step 4 gives ∂A_t = S_t, so M_W(∂A_t) = M_W(S_t) ≤ g(t) by step 6.
9. Conclusion. The family (A_t)_{t∈ℝ} and g satisfy:
 - g is measurable (step 6);
 - for every t, A_t is a restriction of X to {x ∈ U : d(x) < t} (step 4);
 - M_W(∂A_t) ≤ g(t) for t ∈ (a, b) (step 8);
 - ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g ≤ L · M_W(X) (step 7). ∎
proof_key_steps: M_V(0) = 0, so SlicingTheorem applies to the cycle X (d is L-Lipschitz on U) and gives slices S_t with IsSlice X d t S_t.
cycle_slice_boundary: for each t, choose a restriction A_t of X to {x ∈ U : d(x) < t} with ∂A_t = S_t.
(R2) of Submission.iwl_restriction_theory: X has a restriction Rb to the open (hence measurable) band {x ∈ U : a < d(x) < b}.
norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz gives ‖fderiv ℝ d‖ ≤ L. The slicing mass clause then gives a measurable g with M_W(S_t) ≤ g(t) on (a, b) and ∫⁻ g ≤ L·M_W(Rb).
restriction_mass_le gives M_W(Rb) ≤ M_W(X), so ∫⁻ g ≤ L·M_W(X). Also M_W(∂A_t) = M_W(S_t) ≤ g(t).

subproblems.title: Fatou selection of a good level and a bounded subsequence
subproblems.statement: Let g_k : ℝ → [0, ∞] (k ∈ ℕ) be measurable functions, a < b real numbers, C ∈ [0, ∞] with C < ∞ and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g_k(t) dt ≤ C for every k, and E ⊆ ℝ countable. Then there are γ ∈ (a, b) with γ ∉ E, a strictly increasing σ : ℕ → ℕ and G ∈ [0, ∞] with G < ∞ such that g_{σ(k)}(γ) ≤ G for every k.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (g : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (a b : ℝ) (C : ℝ≥0∞) (E : Set ℝ), a < b → (∀ k, Measurable (g k)) → C < ∞ → (∀ k, ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g k t ≤ C) → E.Countable → ∃ (γ : ℝ) (σ : ℕ → ℕ) (G : ℝ≥0∞), γ ∈ Ioo a b ∧ γ ∉ E ∧ StrictMono σ ∧ G < ∞ ∧ ∀ k, g (σ k) γ ≤ G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 6, 7 and 8 of the parent proof. This is the Fatou-lemma form of the selection argument cited in the printed proof of 8.2: “by 4.5(1) and a selection argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2”.

Write λ := volume⌞(a,b) for Lebesgue measure restricted to the open interval (a, b), so that ∫⁻_{(a,b)} h = ∫⁻ h dλ.

1. Define F(t) := liminf_{k→∞} g_k(t) ∈ [0, ∞] for t ∈ ℝ. F is measurable, being the liminf of a sequence of measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions (Measurable.liminf).
2. Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le, for the measure λ and the measurable g_k) gives ∫⁻ F dλ ≤ liminf_k ∫⁻ g_k dλ. Since ∫⁻ g_k dλ ≤ C for every k, and so in particular frequently, liminf_k ∫⁻ g_k dλ ≤ C (liminf_le_of_frequently_le'). Hence ∫⁻ F dλ ≤ C < ∞.
3. F is measurable and ∫⁻ F dλ ≠ ∞, so F(t) < ∞ for λ-a.e. t (ae_lt_top).
4. E is countable and Lebesgue measure on ℝ has no atoms, so volume(E) = 0 (Set.Countable.measure_zero). Equivalently, t ∉ E for volume-a.e. t (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem), and hence also for λ-a.e. t (ae_restrict_of_ae).
5. (a, b) is measurable, so λ-a.e. t lies in (a, b) (ae_restrict_mem).
6. λ ≠ 0. Indeed, λ = 0 would mean volume((a, b)) = 0 (Measure.restrict_eq_zero), but volume((a, b)) = ofReal(b − a) > 0 because a < b (Real.volume_Ioo). Therefore the a.e. filter of λ is nontrivial (ae_neBot). The conjunction of the properties in steps 3, 4 and 5 holds λ-a.e., so it holds at some point (Filter.Eventually.exists): there is γ with F(γ) < ∞, γ ∉ E and γ ∈ (a, b).
7. Put G := F(γ) + 1. Then G < ∞, as a sum of two finite elements of [0, ∞] (ENNReal.add_lt_top). Also F(γ) < G (ENNReal.lt_add_right, since F(γ) ≠ ∞ and 1 ≠ 0).
8. liminf_k g_k(γ) = F(γ) < G, so g_k(γ) < G holds for infinitely many k, i.e. frequently along atTop (Filter.frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt). Its coboundedness side condition holds automatically in the complete lattice [0, ∞].
9. By extraction_of_frequently_atTop, there is a strictly increasing σ : ℕ → ℕ with g_{σ(k)}(γ) < G for every k, and in particular g_{σ(k)}(γ) ≤ G.
10. Thus γ ∈ (a, b), γ ∉ E, σ is strictly increasing, G < ∞, and g_{σ(k)}(γ) ≤ G for all k, as claimed. ∎
proof_key_steps: F := liminf_k g_k is measurable, and Fatou's lemma gives ∫⁻_{(a,b)} F ≤ C < ∞.
F < ∞ a.e. on (a, b); the countable set E is Lebesgue-null; a.e. t (for volume⌞(a,b)) lies in (a, b).
volume((a, b)) > 0 makes the a.e. filter nontrivial, so pick γ ∈ (a, b) ∖ E with F(γ) < ∞.
With G := F(γ) + 1, g_k(γ) < G holds frequently; extract a strictly increasing σ with g_{σ(k)}(γ) ≤ G.
